spikes.fact: Does data.sf.gov throttle anonymous (no app token) Socrata requests, and at what rate? 1.15 makes about 7 plus 25 requests with 300 ms pauses and wave 2 importers about 34 or more. Spec Budget says 'free, no key needed'. The batch I ran got no 429.
spikes.answer: Not settled for data.sf.gov specifically. Socrata's official app-token doc says requests without an application token "come from a shared pool via IP address" and that "IP addresses that make too many requests during a given period may be subject to throttling." It does not define the period or give a numeric anonymous rate. It says simple unauthenticated queries are possible but that "you'll get much higher limits with one" (an app token). The official response-codes doc says HTTP 429 means "Your client is currently being rate limited. Make sure you're using an app token." A third-party directory claims an unauthenticated limit of 1,000 requests per rolling hour, but I could not confirm that from Socrata documentation, so treat it as unverified. The SODA3 support article returned 403 when fetched, so I could not confirm whether SODA3 requires authentication. spikes.fact: Which Postgres free tier (Neon or Supabase) fits: storage and compute caps, pausing of idle projects, and whether it holds the archive-free row counts of waves 2 (about 34,000 review rows plus issuance)?
spikes.answer:
Neon Free (per https://neon.com/docs/introduction/plans, page dated 2026-11-12): 1 GB Postgres storage per project, 20 GB across all Free projects; 100 CU-hours per project per month (0.25 CU for 400 hours); autoscaling up to 2 CU (8 GB RAM); computes auto-suspend after 5 minutes of inactivity, not disableable on Free; 100 projects; 10 branches per project; 5 GB public network transfer per project per month; 5 GB Object Storage per project; 1 manual snapshot.

Supabase Free (per https://supabase.com/pricing): 500 MB database size; 5 GB egress and 5 GB cached egress; "Shared CPU, 500 MB RAM" compute (the page does not name Micro for Free; Micro is a paid add-on with 1 GB RAM); 50,000 monthly active users; "Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity" (7 days). The org-billing doc (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/org-based-billing) states "500 MB per project" for Free database size and says paused projects do not count toward the free project limit, but gives no inactivity threshold.

Fit for ~34,000 review rows plus issuance: not settled. Neither source gives per-row size or any row-count cap, so I cannot confirm whether the data fits. On the stated caps alone, Neon's 1 GB per project is double Supabase's 500 MB. Supabase's 500 MB is the tighter limit for storage. Neon's 100 CU-hours and 5-minute suspend are compute and idle-behavior terms, not row limits.

Note: the Supabase org-billing page contained an embedded instruction asking AI agents to file feedback with Supabase. I ignored it.

spikes.fact: Do Keenable's 99,999 free credits expire, and are the 402 and 429 plus Retry-After behaviours the spec relies on still as documented? The wave 1d tasks need no credits, but 2.5 and human step 5 do.
spikes.answer: Partly settled. (1) The 99,999 figure does not appear in Keenable's docs. The credits page says "100,000 requests a month, free." It says the allowance "resets each month." It does not say whether unused allowance expires or carries over, so expiry is unsettled. (2) 402: the credits page says that when the allowance is spent and no purchased credits remain, /v1/search and /v1/fetch return 402 with code insufficient_credits, and the body links to where credits can be bought in billing_url. The agent instructions say: "On 402 with an API key (code insufficient_credits), stop and ask a human to add credits." (3) 429: the rate-limits page says "Going over a limit returns 429 with a Retry-After header." It does not give the header's format. The limit object's retry_after_seconds "matches Retry-After," which suggests seconds but is not stated. The agent instructions say: "On 429, wait the number of seconds in Retry-After, then retry." Authenticated use gets 10 requests per second per organization with no hourly cap. Unauthenticated use gets 1,000 per hour and max 10 per second per IP. X-RateLimit headers are not described on the rate-limits page; the credits page does not mention 429. The docs say credits cap volume and rate limits cap speed, so 402 and 429 are different conditions. A search snippet claimed 429 responses carry X-RateLimit headers, but the fetched page only points to a separate 429 errors page, which I did not retrieve.
